answer: A beacon signs each key into the tide, locking walnut as surety — forfeited whole if any key it anchors is proven fake — and the bond it must post for each key equals base walnut times its current key count, recomputed every tide. Beacons are attested chips, one per device, and none rent in bulk. A faker's clones cluster on its own beacon, so the k-th clone posts k×base and the fleet freezes k(k+1)/2 × base walnut: capital rising per head, unsharable, unparallelizable. A newcomer on a quiet beacon posts base walnut alone.
